Superstore Analysis — Modular Version

An end-to-end data analysis using modular Python modules.

Superstore Sales Analysis (2015–2018)¶

Tools: Python · Pandas · NumPy · Matplotlib · Seaborn Project Objective This project performs an end-to-end exploratory data analysis of the Superstore retail dataset, covering approximately 10,000 orders from a US-based superstore chain between 2015 and 2018.

The analysis answers five key business questions:

  1. How has sales trended over time? Is there seasonality?
  2. Which product categories and sub-categories drive the most sales and profit?
  3. Which geographic regions perform best?
  4. What is the impact of discounts on profitability?
  5. Which customer segment creates the most value?

Dataset Overview Source: Sample-Superstore.xlsx — a classic retail dataset widely used in data analytics training. Period: January 2015 – December 2018 Scope: Orders, customers, products, regions, sales, profit, and discounts. Key columns: Order Date, Ship Date, Segment, Region, Category, Sub-Category, Sales, Quantity, Discount, Profit. Methodology

The project follows a six-step data analysis workflow:

  1. Problem Definition — formulate business questions
  2. Data Loading — read and inspect the raw dataset
  3. Data Cleaning — remove duplicates, fix dtypes, filter invalid values
  4. Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) — group, aggregate, and trend analysis
  5. Visualization — five key charts + a consolidated dashboard
  6. Reporting— interpretation, business implications, and recommendations Deliverables
  • A fully documented Jupyter Notebook (this file)
  • Five key visualizations consolidated into a single dashboard
  • Structured interpretations with business implications
  • Export to HTML for sharing and a GitHub repository for version control

import pandas as pd
current_dir= os.getcwd()
src_path =os.path.abspath(os.path.join(current_dir,'..')) 
if src_path not in sys.path:
    sys.path.append(src_path)
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import src.visualization as viz

from src.data_loader import load_data
from src.data_cleaning import clean_data
from src.feature_engineering import add_time_features
from src.eda import (
    get_monthly_summary,
    get_category_summary,
    get_region_summary,
    get_segment_summary,
    get_peak_months,
    get_skewnes,
    get_kurtosis,
    analyze_seasonality,
    report_correlation,
    get_top_subcategories
)
%matplotlib inline
sns.set_style("whitegrid")
